I. Order reserved on : 02.05.2025 J. Date of Order : 07.05.2025  K. Final Order : Conviction Brief statement of reasons for decision of the case 1.

It is the case of the prosecution that on 17.10.2014 at about 01.30 PM in the room of W/SI Seema,
PS Mahendra Park, Delhi within jurisdiction of PS Mahendra Park, both the accused in pursuance of their common intention to seek the release of one Vishal from the custody of the complainant,
obstructed the complainant in discharge of her public function and also used criminal force against her to deter her from discharging her duties, thereby committing offences punishable under Section186/353/34 IPC.
2. The charge sheet against both the accused persons was filed in the court on 19.02.2015 upon which cognizance was taken on the same day.
Accused persons appeared before the Court on summons and copy of charge-sheet along with other documents under Section 207 Cr.P.C. was supplied to them.

3. Charge was framed against both the accused persons vide order dated 25.02.2016 for the offences punishable under Section 186/353/34 IPC, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
4. Thereafter, the matter was listed for prosecution evidence wherein the prosecution examined 08 witnesses.

5. PW-1 W/HC Raj Rani deposed that on 17.10.2014, she was posted as HC at PS Mahendra Park and performing her duty from 08 am to 04 PM and at about 01:30 PM, SI Seema alongwith Ct. Ram Niwas brought accused Vishal (accused in other FIR where accused Shalu was complainant) to the police station.
Accused Shalu and Kashmiri started shouting in PS and told SI Seema that they do not want any proceedings against said Vishal.
Thereafter, both accused Shalu and Kashmiri entered the room of SI Seema and started scuffling with her and tried to remove said Vishal from the custody of SI Seema.
PW1 alongwith W/Ct. Neelam took out both the accused from the room of SI Seema and consequently, Inspector C.L. Meena recorded statement of SI Seema in this regard.
Present FIR was registered based on the complaint of SI Seema.

6. PW2 W/Ct. Neelam deposed on the lines of PW1 and submitted that on 17.10.2014, at about 01:30 PM, when SI Seema along with Ct. Ram Niwas arrived at the police station, after the arrest of one Vishal, who was an accused in some other FIR, the present accused persons namely Shalu and Kashmiri started shouting at SI Seema that they do not want any proceedings against said Vishal.
Thereafter, both accused Shalu and Kashmiri entered the room of SI Seema and started scuffling with her and tried to remove said Vishal from the custody of SI Seema.
7. PW3 Ct.

Ram Niwas deposed that on 17.10.2014, he was posted at PS Mahendra Park and he was deputed with SI Seema in investigation of FIR No. 581/2014 u/S 376 IPC and arrested one Vishal and came back to the PS at about 01:30-02:00 PM.

Complainant Shalu (accused in present FIR)
along with her mother Kashmiri (accused in present case) started shouting that they do not want any proceedings against Vishal and followed SI Seema to her room and started mishandling and attempted to release said Vishal from police custody.
Meanwhile, Duty Office W/HC Raja Rani/PW-1 and W/Ct. Neelam/PW-2 came to the spot and removed both the accused out of the room of SI Seema.

8. PW4 SI Seema deposed that on 17.10.2014 she was conducting investigation in case FIR no.
581/2014.

She along with Ct. Ram Niwas (PW-3) arrested an accused namely Vishal in FIR No.
581/2014, PS Mahendra Park u/s 376 IPC and brought him to the police station.

She further deposed that on 17.10.2014, around 1.30PM when she brought Vishal to the police station after arrest, the present accused Ms. Shalu, who was the complainant in FIR no. 581/2014 was already present along with her mother/co-accused Smt. Kashmiri Devi in the police station and on seeing Vishal being brought to the PS after arrest, the two started shouting and yelling at her with the intention to force her to release the accused.
She deposed that the accused persons started shouting that they do not want any proceedings against Vishal and thus they manhandled with her to secure the release of accused Vishal.

She further submitted that upon hearing the noise created by accused persons, DO WHC Raj Rani (PW-1) and W Ct. Neelam came to her room and got hold of the accused persons who were obstructing / preventing her from performing her official duties.

She proved her State vs Shalu on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171965387/
2 statement seeking action against both the accused persons for causing obstruction in performance of her official duties is Ex. PW-4/A.
9.
PW5 Inspector Jatinder Kumar deposed in regards to the investigation carried out by him.
He submitted that on 17.10.2014, investigation of present FIR was handed over to him as SI.
He recorded the statement of officials at PS.
Accused persons were interrogated and a sanction /complaint u/s 195 CrPC Ex. PW-5/A
was obtained by him from ACP Concerned.
Upon completion of investigation, Charge-sheet was prepared without arrest of both the accused persons.

10. PW6 Inspector C.L. Meena deposed that on 17.10.2014, at around 01:25-01:30 PM, he heard some noises coming from the ground floor of the PS and on inspecting, he saw two ladies namely Shalu and Kashmiri were doing hathapai with W/SI Seema.
He recorded statement of W/SI Seema/PW4 and prepared tehrir Ex. PW-6/A and by the direction of SHO, further investigation was marked to SI Jitender.
11. PW7 W/HC Rajni deposed that on 17.10.2014, at about 07:50 AM, she was assigned to made entries in roznamcha B and DD No. 14B Ex. PW-7/A (OSR) was recorded.

12. PW8 Retired ACP Sh. Prem Singh Hooda, was a formal witness who proved the complaint u/s/
195 Cr PC based on which the present FIR was registered.
He deposed that on 10.02.2015, he was working as ACP, Sub Division, Shalimar Bagh.

On that day, SI Jitender Kumar came to his office with case file of FIR No. 648/2014 PS Mahendra Park and on perusal of the same, he filed complaint u/S 195 CrPC Ex. PW-8/A before the court with request to take cognizance against the accused persons.
13. All witnesses were duly cross examined by ld counsel for the accused.
Thereafter, PE was closed.

14. All incriminating evidence was put to the accused persons and their statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded on 20.01.2024 whereby the accused persons submitted that the present case is false and fabricated and that they wish to lead defence evidence.

15. Accused Shalu in his examination as DW1, deposed that on 17.10.2014, she went to PS Mahendra Park with her mother co-accused Kashmiri to request IO/W/SI Seema to ensure that strict action is taken against one Vishal against whom she had gotten a FIR no. 581/2014 u/s 376 IPC registered.
However, the IO falsely implicated her and her mother in the present case.

16. Accused Kashmiri Devi in her examination as DW2 deposed in lines with the testimony of DW1 Shalu and submitted that on 17.10.2014, she went to PS Mahendra Park with her daughter co-accused Shalu to request IO/W/SI Seema to ensure that strict action against Vishal against whom her daughter had gotten a FIR no. 581/2014 u/s 376 IPC registered.
However, the IO falsely implicated both of them mother in the present case alleging assault and obstruction of public duty.
17. Both witnesses were duly cross examined by Ld APP for the State.
NO other witness was sought to be examined in defence, hence DE was closed on State vs Shalu on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171965387/
18. Final arguments heard on behalf of both parties.

19. Before appreciating the evidence, I deem it fit to reproduce and discuss the relevant provisions which are as follows:
20. Section 353. Assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty-

Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person being a public servant in the execution of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person from discharging his duty as such public servant, or in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by such person in the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

21. Section 186 IPC Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions.
Whoever voluntarily obstructs any public servant in the discharge of his public functions, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
In the instant case, the prosecution has examined as many as 08 witnesses to establish its case.
PW-7 and PW-8 are merely formal witnesses who have proved the DD entry, the registration of FIR and the complaint u/s 195 Cr PC.
It is only PW-1, PW-2, PW-3, PW-4, PW-6 and the IO PW-5 whose testimonies are important to determine if the alleged offences have been established by the prosecution beyond doubt.

24. The prime witness i.e. the complainant SI Seema in her testimony as PW-4, submitted that on 17.10.2014, she along with Ct. Ram Niwas (PW-3) arrested an accused namely Vishal in FIR No.
581/2014, PS Mahendra Park u/s 376 IPC and brought him to the police station.

She further State vs Shalu on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171965387/
4 deposed that at around 1.30PM when she brought Vishal to the police station after arrest, the present accused Ms. Shalu, who was the complainant in FIR no. 581/2014 was present along with her mother/co-accused Smt. Kashmiri Devi in the police station and on seeing Vishal being brought to the PS after arrest, the two started shouting and yelling at her with the intention to force her to release the accused.

sentences.text: She deposed that the accused persons started shouting that they do not want any proceedings against Vishal and thus they manhandled with her to secure the release of accused Vishal.

She further submitted that upon hearing the noise created by accused persons, DO WHC Raj Rani (PW-1) and W Ct. Neelam came to her room and got hold of the accused persons who were obstructing / preventing her from performing her official duties.

25. The testimony of witness/ complainant is supported by the deposition of W HC Raj Rani (PW-1)
and W Ct Neelam (PW-2) both of whom have consistently submitted in their respective testimonies that they were on duty in the PS on 17.10.2014.
They have further deposed that at about 1.30PM, SI Seema along with Ct. Ram Niwas brought Vishal in the PS after arrest in FIR No. 581/2014.
They further deposed that both the accused entered the room of SI Seema and started fighting and scuffling with her in order to remove accused Vishal from the custody of SI Seema.

Further, PW-3 Ct Ram Niwas in his testimony has also supported the deposition of the complainant and other witnesses that on 17.10.2014 when he along with SI Seema came to the PS, the present accused persons started shouting at them that they do not want any action against Vishal and that Vishal should be let off.
The witness further submitted that the accused persons started mishandling SI Seema and attempted to secure release of Vishal from police custody.

26. Witness PW-6 Inspector C.L. Meena who was posted as ATO in PS Mahinder Park on the date of incident has also deposed that on 17.10.2014 he saw the present accused persons doing hathapai with the complainant W SI Seema.
Further in his cross-examination, PW-6 has submitted that the ladies were shouting 'iss muljim ko chod do hame case nahi cahiye'.

Thus, witness PW-6 also deposed on the lines of testimonies of witness PW-1 to PW-4.
27.

Though all the witnesses to the offence i.e. PW-1 to PW-4 and PW-5 were duly cross examined by the counsel for the accused, neither any contradiction in their statements inter-se was brought forth nor any contradiction or improvement was observed from their previously recorded statement u/s 161 Cr PC.

All the witnesses have consistently submitted that the accused persons tried to release one Vishal from the custody of the complainant and in such process, they manhandled and scuffled with the complainant SI Seema thereby assaulting her with the intent and further creating obstruction in discharge of her public duty.
28. IO/ PW5 Inspector Jatinder Kumarin
his testimony has detailed the procedure of investigation undertaken by him.

Ld. counsel for the accused in his cross examination as well as in the cross examination of other witnesses has attempted to raise a defence that the prosecution has intentionally not placed on record any CCTV footage of cameras inside the PS.

However, apart from making the said suggestion, the accused has not taken any steps to establish that despite there being CCTV cameras containing the footage of the incident, the prosecution has intentionally not brought the same before this court.

It is not that the accused persons have summoned the record of the central server of the alleged CCTV camera or that they have produced an independent witness who State vs Shalu on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171965387/
5 has deposed in regards to the existence of the same.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Prosecution witnesses PW-1 to PW- 6 all have consistently submitted that there was no CCTV camera at the spot.
On the contrary, the accused persons in their testimonies as DW-1 and DW-2 as well have not made any mention of existence of any CCTV camera installed at or near the spot.

29. Even otherwise, the matter pertains to the year 2014 when the installation of CCTV cameras inside the PS was neither a requirement of law nor was a practice rampantly employed by the police force.

Thus, in absence of any cogent evidence to support existence of any footage of the incident captured by any CCTV camera, no adverse inference can be drawn against the prosecution that they have intentionally not brought any footage before this court only to falsely implicate the accused persons, especially when all the prosecution witnesses have given consistent evidence about the acts of the accused persons.

30. Another defence as contended by ld counsel for the accused during the arguments is that the IO has deliberately not joined any public person present at the spot at the time of incident and in absence of any independent public witness sole testimony of the police official cannot be relied upon.
31.

Perusal of record reveals that while PW-1 and PW-2 have submitted that they cannot say whether any public persons were present at the PS at the time of incident, PW-5 and PW-6 have submitted that while there were public persons in the PS they were asked to join the investigation none of them agreed to do so and they left by citing one reason or another.
It is further admitted by both the witnesses that no written notice or legal action was taken against such public persons.

32. Now there is neither any rule of law nor any presumption of evidence that testimony of police officials is inherently unreliable and that the same cannot be considered in absence of some independent evidence.

Further, it is a matter of common knowledge that public persons are reluctant to be a witness to or to provide assistance to the investigation authorities due to an inherent distrust upon the public system.
33. In the instant case witness PW-1 to PW-6 have given a consistent testimony in regards to the acts of the accused persons.
Ld. counsel for the accused despite having thoroughly cross examined each of the witnesses have failed to raise any doubt upon the veracity of their testimony.

Further no submission has been made as to why all the witnesses who are police officials would depose falsely on oath thereby subjecting themselves to prosecution for the offence of perjury only to false implicate the accused persons with whom they have no previous association whatsoever.

Thus,
simply because the public witnesses have not joined in the proceedings by the IO, the same does not in any way prejudice the case of the prosecution.
34. During arguments Ld. counsel for the accused also submitted that the allegations of assault cannot be said to have been established as the IO did not get the MLC of the complainant conducted.
It is further submitted that the IO also did not collect the uniform of complainant SI Seema.

Record reveals that though the alleged discrepancy in the case of the prosecution was never put by Ld.
counsel for the accused to the IO during his cross-examination to allow him to explain why MLC was State vs Shalu on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171965387/
6 not conducted and why the uniform of the complainant was not seized, IO PW-5 in his cross-examination has specifically submitted that there were no apparent injury marks upon SI Seema.

entities.text: MLC was State vs Shalu on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: None of the other witnesses have deposed in regards to any hurt being caused to SI Seema by the accused persons.
Further there is no submissions that the accused persons torn the uniform of the complainant while they were heckling with her.
In such circumstances, this court finds no reason for the IO to conduct an MLC of the complainant or to seize her uniform as evidence.

35. Even otherwise, for the purpose of offence of assault, there is no requirement to cause any actual injury upon the victim and making of gestures with the intention or knowledge that said gesture would cause such person to whom it is made, to apprehend that the accused is about to use criminal force is sufficient to invite prosecution.

The prosecution witnesses in their testimonies have sufficiently established that the accused persons by manhandling and scuffling with the complainant caused an apprehension in the mind of the complainant and other police officials present that they would use criminal force to deter the complainant from discharging her public function.

Thus,
arguments of Ld counsel for the accused in this regard do not have any force.

36. Now the accused persons in their respective statement u/s 313 Cr PC as well as in their deposition as DW-1 and DW-2 have admitted their presence in the PS on 17.10.2014 and have further submitted that on the said day, they have visited the PS to request the IO to take a strict action against accused Vishal apprehended in FIR no. 581/14, u/s 376 IPC.
They have further submitted that they have been falsely implicated in the present matter by the IO.

However, no submissions have been made as to what strict action, did they intend to request to SI Seema when she had anyways arrested accused Vishal and had brought him to the PS for further interrogation and further proceedings.
37. Further, the accused persons have only made a vague submission that the IO in the present matter has falsely implicated them.

However, no submission has been made as to why the IO who is a police official and is duty bound to protect the legal rights of the citizen would implicate the present accused persons in a false proceedings especially when there is neither any submission in regards to any previous animosity between the IO and the present accused persons nor there is any allegation of any bribe etc.
There is also no submission as to why as many as 08 prosecution witnesses have deposed against them, to prove a case which is alleged to be false.

Further as admitted in their cross-examination, the accused persons have not made any complaint against any police officials or SI Seema for either not taking due action against accused Vishal qua which they have stated to have visited the PS on the un-fateful day or in regards to being falsely implicated in the present FIR.

38. Thus, in view of the consistent testimonies of prosecution witnesses and failure of the accused to establish any defence whatsoever, this court is of the view that prosecution has duly established its case that the accused persons have committed the offence punishable u/s 186/353/34 IPC.
39.
Accordingly, accused Shalu D/o Sh. Jeet Ram and accused Kashmiri S/o Sh. Jeet Ram stand convicted of the offence punishable under Section 186/353/34 IPC.
